verses.original: Διοδεύσαντες δὲ τὴν Ἀμφίπολιν καὶ τὴν Ἀπολλωνίαν ἦλθον εἰς Θεσσαλονίκην ὅπου ἦν συναγωγὴ τῶν Ἰουδαίων
verses.transliteration: Diodeusantes de tēn Amphipolin kai tēn Apollōnian ēlthon eis Thessalonikēn hopou ēn synagōgē tōn Ioudaiōn
verses.literal: When they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia they came to Thessalonica where there was a Jewish synagogue
verses.literalPt: Tendo passado por Anfípolis e Apolônia, chegaram a Tessalônica, onde havia uma sinagoga de judeus.

verses.original: κατὰ δὲ τὸ εἰωθὸς τῷ Παύλῳ εἰσῆλθεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς καὶ ἐπὶ σάββατα τρία διελέξατο αὐτοῖς ἀπὸ τῶν γραφῶν
verses.transliteration: kata de to eiōthos tō Paulō eisēlthen pros autous kai epi sabbata tria dielexato autois apo tōn graphōn
verses.literal: As was his custom Paul went into . . . the synagogue and on three Sabbaths he reasoned with them from the Scriptures
verses.literalPt: Paulo, segundo o seu costume, ali entrou e, por três sábados, discutiu com eles, tirando argumentos das Escrituras,

verses.original: διανοίγων καὶ παρατιθέμενος ὅτι τὸν Χριστὸν ἔδει παθεῖν καὶ ἀναστῆναι ἐκ νεκρῶν καὶ ὅτι Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὃν ἐγὼ καταγγέλλω ὑμῖν
verses.transliteration: dianoigōn kai paratithemenos hoti ton Christon edei pathein kai anastēnai ek nekrōn kai hoti Houtos estin ho Christos ho Iēsous hon egō katangellō hymin
verses.literal: explaining and proving that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead This Jesus I am proclaiming to you is the Christ he declared
verses.literalPt: expondo e demonstrando ser necessário que o Cristo padecesse e ressurgisse dentre os mortos. Este Jesus, que eu vos anuncio, dizia ele, é o Cristo.

verses.original: καί τινες ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐπείσθησαν καὶ προσεκληρώθησαν τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ τῷ Σιλᾷ τῶν τε σεβομένων Ἑλλήνων πλῆθος πολὺ γυναικῶν τε τῶν πρώτων οὐκ ὀλίγαι
verses.transliteration: kai tines ex autōn epeisthēsan kai proseklērōthēsan tō Paulō kai tō Sila tōn te sebomenōn Hellēnōn plēthos poly gynaikōn te tōn prōtōn ouk oligai
verses.literal: Some of the Jews were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas along with a large number of God-fearing Greeks and quite a few leading women
verses.literalPt: Alguns deles ficaram persuadidos e se associaram com Paulo e Silas, bem como uma grande multidão de gregos devotos e não poucas mulheres de qualidade.

verses.original: Ζηλώσαντες δὲ οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ προσλαβόμενοι τῶν ἀγοραίων ἄνδρας τινὰς πονηροὺς καὶ ὀχλοποιήσαντες ἐθορύβουν τὴν πόλιν καὶ ἐπιστάντες τῇ οἰκίᾳ Ἰάσονος ἐζήτουν αὐτοὺς προαγαγεῖν εἰς τὸν δῆμον
verses.transliteration: Zēlōsantes de hoi Ioudaioi kai proslabomenoi tōn agoraiōn andras tinas ponērous kai ochlopoiēsantes ethoryboun tēn polin kai epistantes tē oikia Iasonos ezētoun autous proagagein eis ton dēmon
verses.literal: The Jews however became jealous So they brought in some troublemakers . . . from the marketplace formed a mob and sent the city into an uproar . . . . . . They raided Jason’s house in search of Paul and Silas hoping to bring them out to the people
verses.literalPt: Porém os judeus, movidos de inveja, tomando consigo alguns homens maus dentre o vulgacho e ajuntando a turba, amotinaram a cidade e, assaltando a casa de Jasom, procuravam-nos para os entregar ao povo.

verses.original: μὴ εὑρόντες δὲ αὐτοὺς ἔσυρον Ἰάσονα καί τινας ἀδελφοὺς ἐπὶ τοὺς πολιτάρχας βοῶντες ὅτι Οἱ τὴν οἰκουμένην ἀναστατώσαντες οὗτοι καὶ ἐνθάδε πάρεισιν
verses.transliteration: mē heurontes de autous esyron Iasona kai tinas adelphous epi tous politarchas boōntes hoti Hoi tēn oikoumenēn anastatōsantes houtoi kai enthade pareisin
verses.literal: But when they could not find them they dragged Jason and some other brothers before the city officials shouting These men who have turned the world upside down have now come . . . here
verses.literalPt: Porém, não os achando, levaram a Jasom e alguns irmãos à presença das autoridades da cidade, clamando: Estes que têm transtornado o mundo chegaram também aqui,

verses.original: οὓς ὑποδέδεκται Ἰάσων καὶ οὗτοι πάντες ἀπέναντι τῶν δογμάτων Καίσαρος πράσσουσι βασιλέα ἕτερον λέγοντες εἶναι Ἰησοῦν
verses.transliteration: hous hypodedektai Iasōn kai houtoi pantes apenanti tōn dogmatōn Kaisaros prassousi basilea heteron legontes einai Iēsoun
verses.literal: and Jason has welcomed them into his home . . . They are all defying . . . Caesar’s decrees saying that there is another king named Jesus
verses.literalPt: aos quais Jasom recolheu. Todos eles vão de encontro aos decretos de César, dizendo haver outro rei, que é Jesus.

verses.original: Ἐτάραξαν δὲ τὸν ὄχλον καὶ τοὺς πολιτάρχας ἀκούοντας ταῦτα
verses.transliteration: Etaraxan de ton ochlon kai tous politarchas akouontas tauta
verses.literal: On hearing this the crowd and city officials were greatly disturbed
verses.literalPt: Ao ouvirem isso, ficaram perturbadas a multidão e as autoridades da cidade;

verses.original: καὶ λαβόντες τὸ ἱκανὸν παρὰ τοῦ Ἰάσονος καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν ἀπέλυσαν αὐτούς
verses.transliteration: kai labontes to hikanon para tou Iasonos kai tōn loipōn apelysan autous
verses.literal: And they collected bond from Jason and the others and then released them
verses.literalPt: e, tendo Jasom e os mais prestado fiança, foram soltos.

verses.original: Οἱ δὲ ἀδελφοὶ εὐθέως διὰ νυκτὸς ἐξέπεμψαν τόν τε Παῦλον καὶ τὸν Σιλᾶν εἰς Βέροιαν οἵτινες παραγενόμενοι εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἀπῄεσαν
verses.transliteration: Hoi de adelphoi eutheōs dia nyktos exepempsan ton te Paulon kai ton Silan eis Beroian hoitines paragenomenoi eis tēn synagōgēn tōn Ioudaiōn apēesan
verses.literal: As soon as night had fallen the brothers sent - Paul and Silas away to Berea On arriving there they went into the Jewish synagogue
verses.literalPt: Logo pela noite, os irmãos enviaram a Paulo e Silas para Bereia; e, tendo eles aí chegado, foram à sinagoga dos judeus.

verses.original: οὗτοι δὲ ἦσαν εὐγενέστεροι τῶν ἐν Θεσσαλονίκῃ οἵτινες ἐδέξαντο τὸν λόγον μετὰ πάσης προθυμίας τὸ καθ’ ἡμέραν ἀνακρίνοντες τὰς γραφὰς εἰ ἔχοι ταῦτα οὕτως
verses.transliteration: houtoi de ēsan eugenesteroi tōn en Thessalonikē hoitines edexanto ton logon meta pasēs prothymias to kath’ hēmeran anakrinontes tas graphas ei echoi tauta houtōs
verses.literal: Now the Bereans were more noble-minded than the Thessalonians for they received the message with great eagerness and examined the Scriptures every day to see if these teachings were true
verses.literalPt: Ora, estes eram mais nobres do que os de Tessalônica, porque receberam a palavra com toda a avidez, indagando diariamente nas Escrituras se essas coisas eram assim.

verses.original: πολλοὶ μὲν οὖν ἐξ αὐτῶν ἐπίστευσαν καὶ τῶν Ἑλληνίδων γυναικῶν τῶν εὐσχημόνων καὶ ἀνδρῶν οὐκ ὀλίγοι
verses.transliteration: polloi men oun ex autōn episteusan kai tōn Hellēnidōn gynaikōn tōn euschēmonōn kai andrōn ouk oligoi
verses.literal: As a result many of them believed along with quite a few prominent Greek women and men
verses.literalPt: Muitos deles creram, bem como não poucas mulheres gregas de boa posição e homens.

verses.original: Ὡς δὲ ἔγνωσαν οἱ ἀπὸ τῆς Θεσσαλονίκης Ἰουδαῖοι ὅτι καὶ ἐν τῇ Βεροίᾳ κατηγγέλη ὑπὸ τοῦ Παύλου ὁ λόγος τοῦ Θεοῦ ἦλθον κἀκεῖ σαλεύοντες καὶ ταράσσοντες τοὺς ὄχλους
verses.transliteration: Hōs de egnōsan hoi apo tēs Thessalonikēs Ioudaioi hoti kai en tē Beroia katēngelē hypo tou Paulou ho logos tou Theou ēlthon kakei saleuontes kai tarassontes tous ochlous
verses.literal: But when the Jews from Thessalonica learned that Paul was also proclaiming the word of God in Berea they went there themselves to incite and agitate the crowds
verses.literalPt: Quando os judeus de Tessalônica souberam que também em Bereia era anunciada por Paulo a palavra de Deus, foram lá excitar e perturbar o povo.

verses.original: εὐθέως δὲ τότε τὸν Παῦλον ἐξαπέστειλαν οἱ ἀδελφοὶ πορεύεσθαι ἕως ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν ὑπέμεινάν τε ὅ τε Σιλᾶς καὶ ὁ Τιμόθεος ἐκεῖ
verses.transliteration: eutheōs de tote ton Paulon exapesteilan hoi adelphoi poreuesthai heōs epi tēn thalassan hypemeinan te ho te Silas kai ho Timotheos ekei
verses.literal: The brothers immediately sent Paul to - the coast but - Silas and Timothy remained in Berea
verses.literalPt: Então, os irmãos fizeram logo sair a Paulo para que fosse até o mar. Porém Silas e Timóteo ficaram ali.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ καθιστάνοντες τὸν Παῦλον ἤγαγον ἕως Ἀθηνῶν καὶ λαβόντες ἐντολὴν πρὸς τὸν Σιλᾶν καὶ τὸν Τιμόθεον ἵνα ὡς τάχιστα ἔλθωσιν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐξῄεσαν
verses.transliteration: hoi de kathistanontes ton Paulon ēgagon heōs Athēnōn kai labontes entolēn pros ton Silan kai ton Timotheon hina hōs tachista elthōsin pros auton exēesan
verses.literal: Those who escorted Paul brought him to Athens and then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join . . . him as soon as possible
verses.literalPt: Os que conduziam a Paulo levaram-no até Atenas e, tendo eles recebido ordem para comunicar a Silas e Timóteo que fossem ter com ele o mais depressa possível, partiram.

verses.original: Ἐν δὲ ταῖς Ἀθήναις ἐκδεχομένου αὐτοὺς τοῦ Παύλου παρωξύνετο τὸ πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ θεωροῦντος κατείδωλον οὖσαν τὴν πόλιν
verses.transliteration: En de tais Athēnais ekdechomenou autous tou Paulou parōxyneto to pneuma autou en autō theōrountos kateidōlon ousan tēn polin
verses.literal: While Paul was waiting for them in Athens he was deeply disturbed in his spirit to see that the city was full of idols
verses.literalPt: Enquanto Paulo os esperava em Atenas, o seu espírito revoltava-se dentro de si mesmo, vendo a cidade cheia de ídolos.

verses.original: διελέγετο μὲν οὖν ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις καὶ τοῖς σεβομένοις καὶ ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ κατὰ πᾶσαν ἡμέραν πρὸς τοὺς παρατυγχάνοντας
verses.transliteration: dielegeto men oun en tē synagōgē tois Ioudaiois kai tois sebomenois kai en tē agora kata pasan hēmeran pros tous paratynchanontas
verses.literal: So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and God-fearing Gentiles and in the marketplace with those he met each day
verses.literalPt: Assim, na sinagoga, discutia ele com os judeus e com os que temiam a Deus e, na praça, todos os dias, discutia com os que ali se achavam.

verses.original: Τινὲς δὲ καὶ τῶν Ἐπικουρείων καὶ Στοϊκῶν φιλοσόφων συνέβαλλον αὐτῷ καί τινες ἔλεγον Τί ἂν θέλοι ὁ σπερμολόγος οὗτος λέγειν οἱ δέ Ξένων δαιμονίων δοκεῖ καταγγελεὺς εἶναι ὅτι τὸν Ἰησοῦν καὶ τὴν ἀνάστασιν εὐηγγελίζετο
verses.transliteration: Tines de kai tōn Epikoureiōn kai Stoikōn philosophōn syneballon autō kai tines elegon Ti an theloi ho spermologos houtos legein hoi de Xenōn daimoniōn dokei katangeleus einai hoti ton Iēsoun kai tēn anastasin euēngelizeto
verses.literal: Some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also began to debate with him Some of them asked What . . . is this babbler trying to say Others said He seems to be advocating foreign gods They said this because Paul was proclaiming the good news of Jesus and the resurrection
verses.literalPt: Mas alguns filósofos epicureus e estoicos contendiam com ele, e uns diziam: Que quererá dizer este paroleiro? E outros: Parece ser proclamador de deuses estranhos; pois pregava a Jesus e a ressurreição.

verses.original: Ἐπιλαβόμενοί τε αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν Ἄρειον πάγον ἤγαγον λέγοντες Δυνάμεθα γνῶναι τίς ἡ καινὴ αὕτη ἡ ὑπὸ σοῦ λαλουμένη διδαχή
verses.transliteration: Epilabomenoi te autou epi ton Areion pagon ēgagon legontes Dynametha gnōnai tis hē kainē hautē hē hypo sou laloumenē didachē
verses.literal: So they took Paul and brought him to the Areopagus . . . where they asked him May we know what this new teaching is that you are presenting
verses.literalPt: Segurando-o, levaram-no ao Areópago, dizendo: Podemos saber que nova doutrina é esta que anuncias?

verses.original: ξενίζοντα γάρ τινα εἰσφέρεις εἰς τὰς ἀκοὰς ἡμῶν βουλόμεθα οὖν γνῶναι τίνα θέλει ταῦτα εἶναι
verses.transliteration: xenizonta gar tina eisphereis eis tas akoas hēmōn boulometha oun gnōnai tina thelei tauta einai
verses.literal: For you are bringing some strange notions to our ears and we want to know what they mean . . .
verses.literalPt: Pois tu nos trazes aos ouvidos coisas estranhas; queremos saber que vem a ser isso.

verses.original: Ἀθηναῖοι δὲ πάντες καὶ οἱ ἐπιδημοῦντες ξένοι εἰς οὐδὲν ἕτερον ηὐκαίρουν ἢ λέγειν τι ἢ ἀκούειν τι καινότερον
verses.transliteration: Athēnaioi de pantes kai hoi epidēmountes xenoi eis ouden heteron ēukairoun ē legein ti ē akouein ti kainoteron
verses.literal: Now all the Athenians and foreigners who lived there spent their time doing nothing more than hearing and articulating - new ideas
verses.literalPt: Ora, todos os atenienses e os estrangeiros que ali moravam não se ocupavam em outra coisa senão em contar ou em ouvir alguma novidade.

verses.original: Σταθεὶς δὲ ὁ Παῦλος ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ Ἀρείου Πάγου ἔφη Ἄνδρες Ἀθηναῖοι κατὰ πάντα ὡς δεισιδαιμονεστέρους ὑμᾶς θεωρῶ
verses.transliteration: Statheis de ho Paulos en mesō tou Areiou Pagou ephē Andres Athēnaioi kata panta hōs deisidaimonesterous hymas theōrō
verses.literal: Then Paul stood up in the meeting of the Areopagus . . . and said Men of Athens I see that in every way you are very religious
verses.literalPt: Paulo, posto em pé no meio do Areópago, disse: Atenienses, em tudo vos vejo muitíssimo tementes aos deuses.

verses.original: διερχόμενος γὰρ καὶ ἀναθεωρῶν τὰ σεβάσματα ὑμῶν εὗρον καὶ βωμὸν ἐν ᾧ ἐπεγέγραπτο ΑΓΝΩΣΤΩ ΘΕΩ Ὃ οὖν ἀγνοοῦντες εὐσεβεῖτε τοῦτο ἐγὼ καταγγέλλω ὑμῖν
verses.transliteration: dierchomenos gar kai anatheōrōn ta sebasmata hymōn heuron kai bōmon en hō epegegrapto AGNŌSTŌ THEŌ Ho oun agnoountes eusebeite touto egō katangellō hymin
verses.literal: For as I walked around and examined your objects of worship I even found . . . an altar with this inscription TO AN UNKNOWN GOD Therefore what you worship as something unknown I now proclaim to you
verses.literalPt: Pois, passando e observando os objetos do vosso culto, achei um altar em que estava escrito: AO DEUS DESCONHECIDO. O que, pois, adorais sem o conhecer é o que eu vos anuncio.

verses.original: Ὁ Θεὸς ὁ ποιήσας τὸν κόσμον καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ οὗτος οὐρανοῦ καὶ γῆς ὑπάρχων Κύριος οὐκ ἐν χειροποιήτοις ναοῖς κατοικεῖ
verses.transliteration: Ho Theos ho poiēsas ton kosmon kai panta ta en autō houtos ouranou kai gēs hyparchōn Kyrios ouk en cheiropoiētois naois katoikei
verses.literal: The God who made the world and everything in it is the Lord of heaven and earth and does not live in temples made by human hands
verses.literalPt: O Deus que fez o mundo e tudo o que nele há, sendo ele o Senhor do céu e da terra, não habita em santuários feitos por mãos dos homens,

verses.original: οὐδὲ ὑπὸ χειρῶν ἀνθρωπίνων θεραπεύεται προσδεόμενός τινος αὐτὸς διδοὺς πᾶσι ζωὴν καὶ πνοὴν καὶ τὰ πάντα
verses.transliteration: oude hypo cheirōn anthrōpinōn therapeuetai prosdeomenos tinos autos didous pasi zōēn kai pnoēn kai ta panta
verses.literal: Nor is He served by human hands as if He needed anything because He Himself gives everyone life and breath and everything else
verses.literalPt: nem é servido por mãos humanas, como se necessitasse de alguma coisa, visto ele mesmo dar a todos vida, respiração e todas as coisas;

verses.original: ἐποίησέν τε ἐξ ἑνὸς πᾶν ἔθνος ἀνθρώπων κατοικεῖν ἐπὶ παντὸς προσώπου τῆς γῆς ὁρίσας προστεταγμένους καιροὺς καὶ τὰς ὁροθεσίας τῆς κατοικίας αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: epoiēsen te ex henos pan ethnos anthrōpōn katoikein epi pantos prosōpou tēs gēs horisas prostetagmenous kairous kai tas horothesias tēs katoikias autōn
verses.literal: From one man He made every nation of men that they should inhabit . . . the whole . . . earth and He determined their appointed times and the boundaries of their lands
verses.literalPt: e de um só fez todo o gênero humano para habitar sobre toda a face da terra, havendo fixado os seus tempos determinados e os limites da sua habitação;

verses.original: ζητεῖν τὸν Θεὸν εἰ ἄρα γε ψηλαφήσειαν αὐτὸν καὶ εὕροιεν καί γε οὐ μακρὰν ἀπὸ ἑνὸς ἑκάστου ἡμῶν ὑπάρχοντα
verses.transliteration: zētein ton Theon ei ara ge psēlaphēseian auton kai heuroien kai ge ou makran apo henos hekastou hēmōn hyparchonta
verses.literal: God intended that they would seek Him and perhaps reach out for Him and find Him though . . . He is not far from each one of us
verses.literalPt: para buscarem a Deus, se, porventura, apalpando, o achassem, ainda que não esteja longe de cada um de nós.

verses.original: Ἐν αὐτῷ γὰρ ζῶμεν καὶ κινούμεθα καὶ ἐσμέν ὡς καί τινες τῶν καθ’ ὑμᾶς ποιητῶν εἰρήκασιν Τοῦ γὰρ καὶ γένος ἐσμέν
verses.transliteration: En autō gar zōmen kai kinoumetha kai esmen hōs kai tines tōn kath’ hymas poiētōn eirēkasin Tou gar kai genos esmen
verses.literal: For in Him we live and move and have our being As some of your own poets have said We are His offspring
verses.literalPt: Pois nele vivemos, e nos movemos, e existimos, como até alguns dos vossos poetas o têm dito: Porque dele também somos geração.

verses.original: γένος οὖν ὑπάρχοντες τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐκ ὀφείλομεν νομίζειν χρυσῷ ἢ ἀργύρῳ ἢ λίθῳ χαράγματι τέχνης καὶ ἐνθυμήσεως ἀνθρώπου τὸ Θεῖον εἶναι ὅμοιον
verses.transliteration: genos oun hyparchontes tou Theou ouk opheilomen nomizein chrysō ē argyrō ē lithō charagmati technēs kai enthymēseōs anthrōpou to Theion einai homoion
verses.literal: Therefore being offspring of God we should not think that the Divine Being is like gold or silver or stone an image formed by man’s skill and imagination
verses.literalPt: Sendo, pois, geração de Deus, não devemos pensar que a divindade é semelhante ao ouro, ou à prata, ou à pedra lavrada por arte e gênio do homem.

verses.original: Τοὺς μὲν οὖν χρόνους τῆς ἀγνοίας ὑπεριδὼν ὁ Θεὸς τὰ νῦν παραγγέλλει τοῖς ἀνθρώποις πάντας πανταχοῦ μετανοεῖν
verses.transliteration: Tous men oun chronous tēs agnoias hyperidōn ho Theos ta nyn parangellei tois anthrōpois pantas pantachou metanoein
verses.literal: Although God overlooked the ignorance of earlier times He now commands all people everywhere to repent
verses.literalPt: Dissimulando, pois, os tempos da ignorância, Deus manda agora que todos os homens, em todo lugar, se arrependam,

verses.original: καθότι ἔστησεν ἡμέραν ἐν ᾗ μέλλει κρίνειν τὴν οἰκουμένην ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ ἐν ἀνδρὶ ᾧ ὥρισεν πίστιν παρασχὼν πᾶσιν ἀναστήσας αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν
verses.transliteration: kathoti estēsen hēmeran en hē mellei krinein tēn oikoumenēn en dikaiosynē en andri hō hōrisen pistin paraschōn pasin anastēsas auton ek nekrōn
verses.literal: For He has set a day when He will judge the world with justice by the Man He has appointed He has given proof of this to everyone by raising Him from the dead
verses.literalPt: porquanto tem fixado um dia em que há de julgar o mundo com justiça, pelo varão que para isso destinou, do que tem dado certeza a todos, ressuscitando-o dentre os mortos.

verses.original: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ ἀνάστασιν νεκρῶν οἱ μὲν ἐχλεύαζον οἱ δὲ εἶπαν Ἀκουσόμεθά σου περὶ τούτου καὶ πάλιν
verses.transliteration: Akousantes de anastasin nekrōn hoi men echleuazon hoi de eipan Akousometha sou peri toutou kai palin
verses.literal: When they heard about the resurrection of the dead some began to mock him but others said We want to hear you again . . . on this topic
verses.literalPt: Mas, quando ouviram falar da ressurreição dos mortos, uns zombavam, e outros diziam: Sobre isso te ouviremos ainda outra vez.

verses.original: οὕτως ὁ Παῦλος ἐξῆλθεν ἐκ μέσου αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: houtōs ho Paulos exēlthen ek mesou autōn
verses.literal: At that Paul left the Areopagus
verses.literalPt: Assim, Paulo saiu do meio deles.

verses.original: τινὲς δὲ ἄνδρες κολληθέντες αὐτῷ ἐπίστευσαν ἐν οἷς καὶ Διονύσιος ὁ Ἀρεοπαγίτης καὶ γυνὴ ὀνόματι Δάμαρις καὶ ἕτεροι σὺν αὐτοῖς
verses.transliteration: tines de andres kollēthentes autō episteusan en hois kai Dionysios ho Areopagitēs kai gynē onomati Damaris kai heteroi syn autois
verses.literal: But some joined him and believed including . . . . . . Dionysius the Areopagite a woman named Damaris and others who were with them
verses.literalPt: Porém alguns homens agregaram-se a ele e creram; entre os quais, Dionísio, o areopagita, e uma mulher chamada Dâmaris, e, com eles, outros.
